A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CMI-RewardBench study. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial appendix additions and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original reward-model evaluations, training ablations, human-preference analyses, and best-of-N generation experiments, including Tables 2–5 and Figure 3.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds test-set re-annotation, teacher-source and architecture ablations, a transcription-based comparison, and generator rankings.

M1.justification: The proposed CMI-RM retains frozen MuQ-MuLan encoders, prompt and joint Transformers, two scoring heads, and the same two-stage training objectives and reranking procedure. New head sizes, Flan-T5 substitution, and mixed-teacher supervision are investigated as ablation variants; they do not replace the proposed pipeline.

E1.justification: The represented datasets and tasks remain CMI-Pref-Pseudo, CMI-Pref, PAM, MusicEval, Music Arena, and MusicCaps, covering musicality and text/lyrics/reference-audio alignment. AIME and MusicPref are added to descriptive comparisons but explicitly excluded from benchmark testing. The transcription analysis and generator leaderboard reuse existing data and conditioning scenarios.

E2.justification: v3 adds Omni-Reward to the main musicality and alignment comparisons and corresponding appendix breakdowns. Appendix I.1 additionally compares Whisper-derived WER preference prediction with CMI-RM on lyric-conditioned pairs. Existing comparators are retained, making this a focused expansion.

E3.justification: Table 4 changes Music Arena prediction from the combined musicality-plus-alignment score to musicality alone. Added experiments introduce 70k-Qwen/40k-Gemini supervision, three reward-head sizes, Flan-T5 substitution, WER tie exclusion, and prompt-wise round-robin generator ranking. These substantially expand experimental protocols. H.2 reports 2,800 objective-reranking prompts while Section 3.3.3 retains 2,183, leaving that sample count unresolved.

E4.justification: v3 adds substantial checks of teacher dependence, mixed pseudo-label sources, model capacity, text-encoder substitution, and transcription as a preference proxy. It also analyzes listening behavior and re-annotates the test set to assess reliability. Earlier smoothing, data-size, mapping, prompt-conditioning, duration, and subgroup analyses remain, sometimes relocated or consolidated.

E5.justification: Beyond v1's agreement statistics and descriptive reporting, v3 adds Wilson 95% confidence intervals for test-label agreement, benchmark significance checks in H.1, and listening-test p-values with an explicitly stated one-sided binomial procedure in H.2. The benchmark test procedure is not specified, and some associated accuracies conflict with tables. No increase in reward-model training seeds or repeated runs is documented.

E6.justification: Most retained headline scores are unchanged, but v3 substantially expands results with Omni-Reward, re-annotation agreement, teacher and architecture ablations, WER prediction, and generator rankings. Table 4's Distill+Both Music Arena accuracy changes from 72.46% to 73.43% under the revised scoring rule, not a demonstrated same-setting gain. New results include 75.0% alignment and 75.2% musicality re-annotation agreement and 60.0% WER-based accuracy on 225 non-tied comparisons.

T1.justification: The model equations, Bradley–Terry formulation, regression mapping, and label-smoothing mathematics are retained. Equation 4 merely rewrites equal loss weights as an equivalent average. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs, and v3's additions concern empirical evaluation rather than new formal theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: two preference datasets, a unified compositional benchmark, a parameter-efficient reward model competitive with specialized baselines, and useful best-of-N filtering. Added analyses support these claims without materially changing their scope.

C2.justification: New Appendix D explicitly discusses reward-hacking limitations, incomplete separation of the scoring heads, and genre/language biases. The contextual-musicality discussion expands the earlier taste-anchor explanation into alternative hypotheses involving human judgment entanglement and statistical shortcuts. New ablation interpretations address teacher dependence and cross-modal fusion bottlenecks, substantially broadening applicability and mechanism discussion.

D1.justification: v3 adds a direct model-weights link and discloses listening-study counts of 50 prompts, 200 generations, and 300 comparisons. It documents configurations for the new ablations, transcription tie handling, and per-generator sample counts and ranking aggregation. The core implementation description and complete LLM-judge prompts are retained; several sample-count descriptions remain inconsistent.

R1.justification: v3 introduces Omni-Reward as a general-purpose reward-model comparator and expands positioning against AIME, MusicPref, and SongEval, explaining their exclusion from the benchmark test sets. The central research gap remains unchanged. Numerous other reference edits correct or update citations for already-discussed models rather than introduce new research directions.

P1.justification: v3 substantially revises the presentation of existing material: it clarifies training versus benchmarking data, compresses benchmark discussion and the conclusion, reorganizes appendix sections, and rewrites the contextual-musicality narrative. It also consolidates duplicated Music Arena discussion and adds a conflict-of-interest disclosure. These changes extend beyond inserting new experimental content.

P2.justification: v3 adds duration/listening-time histograms and a scatterplot, plus tables for reliability, new ablations, significance checks, and generator leaderboards. Table 1 gains dataset columns and an official-split row, while comparison tables gain Omni-Reward rows. The duplicated Music Arena regression table is consolidated. Existing main diagrams and preference heatmaps are retained, with caption and placement changes.

improvement.justification: v3 provides more direct checks of benchmark reliability and teacher dependence, broader ablations, an additional relevant baseline, and clearer limitations. These improve the paper's evidential transparency. However, new inconsistencies limit the gain: H.1 reports 78.60% for the CMI-Pref model while Table 2 reports 77.80%, and A.3 describes four re-annotators while Table 7 specifies three. Conflicting reranking sample counts further weaken reproducibility. The net improvement is supported but limited.
